title: DataBall wide CSV appends must apply the CSV schema before merging
lead: Appending a CSV with a unit header (`Gain(dB)`) to a wide session that already has `Gain` throws `Duplicate canonical column 'Gain' from header 'Gain(dB)'`.

The cause: a wide session applies the CSV schema (header canonicalization, configured types, metadata extraction) to the whole `"data"` table *after* the merge (`ImportCsvWithSchema`, `src/DataBall/DataBall.cs`). The raw header `Gain(dB)` therefore lands as a new column next to `Gain`, and canonicalizing it collides. Layout sessions already apply the schema to staging before routing.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** schema merge and widening rules (db-23); many-file opens (db-11).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Found during the db-22 relay and confirmed on base 7c17c59. Owner, 2026-10-11: track it separately from db-23 to keep db-23 small. db-11 opens many CSVs and will hit this, so db-11 depends on this item.

**Model note:** Claude-only. The implementer is Sonnet 5.5 at high effort, because CSV schema ordering is subtle.

**Verify first, in spec review:**
- which tests depend on the current order (header renames and metadata extraction over the whole table after the merge);
- whether applying the schema on staging changes wide-session behavior that README "Differences from a wide session" documents.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/DataBall/DataBall.cs` (`ImportCsvWithSchema`, `ApplyCsvSchema`): for wide sessions, apply the schema to staging before the merge, as layout sessions do.
- README and `docs/how-it-works.md`, if wide/layout differences change.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `WideAppend_UnitHeader_MergesIntoCanonicalColumn`: `a.csv` has `Gain`; appending `b.csv` with `Gain(dB)` yields one `Gain` column and no throw.
2. Existing wide CSV tests stay green; list any whose expectations change.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Spec review.
2. `slicer start`. Write the tests and watch them fail.
3. Implement, mutation-check, run the full suite and the format check.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build DataBall.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test DataBall.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format DataBall.sln --verify-no-changes`
- `slicer check`
